root.description: The id of the root the path is under

path.description: The declaring member's package.json, relative to its root

name.description: The dependency's key in that field

targetPath.description: The package.json of the workspace member the dependency names, a structural fact and never an install outcome: for a `workspace:` path, `file:`, `link:` or a bare path the manager reads as one, the member at that directory; for anything else, the member whose name is the dependency's name (`npm:<name>@`, and pnpm's and bun's `workspace:<name>@`, name `<name>`; npm names a member with no `name` by its folder), the root only where the manager lets a name reach it, and under bun a member sharing the root's name before the root. No version is checked and no registry, catalog or link setting is read. Null when it names no one member: no member carries the name, two do (WORKSPACE_DUPLICATE_NAME), the path holds no member or is a bun link registration (WORKSPACE_PATH_UNRESOLVED), or the answer depends on an unknown manager (WORKSPACE_MANAGER_UNKNOWN). While a member's name is unknown (WORKSPACE_TARGET_UNKNOWN, once per root) every name match in the root is uncertain, null or not

protocol.description: `workspace`: a `workspace:` range; `catalog`: a `catalog:` range; `link` and `file`: a `link:` or `file:` path, or a bare path (no protocol prefix) the manager reads as a directory or tarball, labelled as the manager reads it (pnpm: `link` for a directory, `file` for a tarball; every other manager, and an unknown one, `file`); `npm`: anything else (a semver range, a tag, an `npm:` alias, a git or tarball URL). The protocol as written, so a check can judge policy over it: VAT does not decide what an install would make of it

projection-workspace-dependencies.description: A row of the derived `workspace_dependencies` relation
